archetypes.name: harness-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan makes very specific structural claims about existing helpers, line ranges, and test patterns that could be wrong and would cause the implementer to anchor changes in the wrong place.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan cites precise structural claims: `make_find_symlink_race_stub` at approximately line 142 of `scripts/test-design-log-publish.sh`, `append_tool_failure_local` and its fallback relay at `ship-pr.sh:~894-901`, and the T8 BEL/ESC fixture at `scripts/test-ci-failed-jobs.sh:178-194`. Verify that each referenced function name, helper stub, and structural anchor actually exists at or near the stated location in the current scope files, and flag any case where a plan instruction ('add sibling helper near line N' or 'after existing check at ~line Y') would land in the wrong place or reference a nonexistent anchor. Check specifically whether the plan-review allowlist ordering claim holds in `design-log-publish.sh`: that the `rel`-regex plus artifact-basename checks fire before both the leaf `[ -L ]` recheck and the proposed ancestor guard in the plan-review loop. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: relay-site-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan classifies relay sites HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW and routes only some; a misclassification or omission leaves a control-byte injection path open while the plan claims closure.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan partitions external-content relay sites into HIGH sites to be routed (ship-pr.sh, collect-findings.sh), MEDIUM sites routed for defense-in-depth (collect-agent-results.sh, review-core.sh), and approximately 40 LOW sites explicitly excluded; verify that this classification is internally consistent by checking whether any relay in the scope files forwards content that can originate from CI, vendor, or external-reviewer output but is classified LOW without documented justification. Check whether the planned `lib-quiet.md` audit subsection's claimed site list matches the actual set of files being changed by the plan, and flag any discrepancy between what the plan says will be documented and what will actually be modified. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: ancestor-guard-logic
archetypes.rationale: Item A's proposed cd+pwd-P+case containment check is the core security fix; if the helper logic has a gap the TOCTOU race remains open despite the plan claiming it is closed.
archetypes.prompt_body: Item A proposes closing the parent-directory TOCTOU race by re-resolving each staged file's parent via `cd "$(dirname "$f")" && pwd -P` and matching against the physical root with a `case` statement; examine whether this logic correctly handles all three named subtrees (plan-review, render-cache, `.completed`) given the plan's own edge cases: a file whose dirname equals the root exactly (no trailing slash), an ancestor symlink whose target resolves back inside the root (should pass), and a `cd` failure returning non-zero (should fail closed). Check whether the plan's instruction to place the ancestor guard after the existing leaf `[ -L "$f" ]` check creates any ordering gap where the ancestor guard could be reached for a leaf symlink that should have been rejected earlier, or conversely where a leaf-rejected file escapes the ancestor check entirely. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
